newsitem.title: USA: Synetic to buy Intranet company.
newsitem.headline: Synetic to buy Intranet company.

text.p: Synetic Inc. said Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Avicenna Systems Corp., which creates so-called intranet internal computer networks for managed health care plans, healthcare delivery systems and hospitals, for $30.5 million in stock.
Under the agreement, Synetic will acquire all of Cambridge, Mass.-based Avicenna's outstanding equity and debt, including employee stock options.
Synetic's stock edged down 6.25 cents to $52.50 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.

"Avicenna provides us with an organisation with a common vision for confidential, secure Internet healthcare commerce, and a talented management team with relevant experience," said said Martin Wygod, chairman of Synetic.
Avicenna's intranet systems allow managed care organisations and provider groups to exchange transaction, procedural, patient outcome and educational information, Synetic said.
Synetic also said it entered into arrangements with key members of Avicenna's management team regarding their equity stakes, to assure their continuation with the company.
